findings.statement: TNFa pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (t [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.t_nr_vs_r=4.79]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), but not in PURSUIT placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]); in the data it is associated with general severity, not a drug-specific mechanism. NFkB shows the same pattern.

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab, but not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); golimumab is also non-significant.

TGFb pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not in golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); UNIFI placebo is also significant, so part of the signal is severity.

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the drug-vs-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]) and UNIFI placebo trends the same way without surviving correction (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]). No other arm survives correction: this is a severity marker, not evidence of a ustekinumab-specific mechanism.

TREM1 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]), indicating severity rather than a drug-specific signal; golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab do not survive correction.

IL11 is the strongest ustekinumab-arm association among the targets checked (BH padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]), but UNIFI placebo non-responders also have higher IL11 (padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]) and the interaction is not significant; it marks severity.

Baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); the drug target's own expression does not separate its responders, and no other arm is significant.

Baseline ITGB7 is not associated with vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]); nothing survives correction in any arm, so no target-expression biomarker for vedolizumab emerges (the vedolizumab arm is small).

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking (clinical-stage antagonists exist) and is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]), but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), so the response association reflects severity (neutrophil-driven inflammation) rather than a drug-specific mechanism.

CXCL8 is among the top convergence-ranked genes and is higher in non-responders in the ustekinumab arm and UNIFI placebo, but golimumab does not survive correction (BH padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]); the signal is not specific to one drug.

CHRDL2 is the top first-in-class candidate and is made mostly by stromal cells (lineage share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939], mainly inflammatory fibroblasts), but only a minority of its increase is retained after composition correction (retained fraction [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.276]) and its highest vital-organ RNA is [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM, a safety flag.

CPXM1 is stromal in both single-cell datasets (lineage share [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.873]), but only a minority of the increase is retained after composition adjustment (retained fraction [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.414]); partly a fibroblast-expansion signal. Missing: functional and genetic support, and any response association.

LAX1 comes mainly from plasma cells in inflamed mucosa (transcript share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.433]); the second dataset assigns it to plasma rather than T/NK, so lineage is not replicated, and the retained fraction is low ([gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.230]). Likely an infiltrating-immune-cell signal; vital-organ RNA is low.

XKR9 is the only top candidate classified as intrinsic to the tissue, epithelial, with most of its increase retained after composition correction (retained fraction [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.798]); however it is up in only a few cohorts and few cells express it, so replication and cellular evidence are weak.

caveats: Pathway and gene associations are baseline biopsy associations, not predictions; the infliximab (small n) and vedolizumab arms are underpowered and the golimumab arm shows no significance for any gene tested.
Ustekinumab (UNIFI) has by far the largest sample size, so its significance partly reflects power; drug-vs-placebo interactions are non-significant for all genes checked.
Most first-in-class discovery candidates are only partly composition-independent and lack genetic or functional support; tractability here is predicted antibody-accessibility only.
Single-cell shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance.
